top_choice_rationale: P001 (Autor, Dorn, Hanson) rests on a first-order question, who bears the adjustment costs of trade, answered with transparent local-labour-market designs that have been replicated and challenged for about a decade. The sign and local concentration of the adjustment costs have survived in qualified form, while long-run magnitudes remain debated. The citation should therefore credit the exposure and adjustment evidence and claim no effect size or task-framework origin. Attribution is tight because the three jointly authored the core programme. I do not treat the ten-member support count as evidence of merit, since much of it came from revisions during round 1. P002 (Helpman, Melitz) is mature and cleanly credited as a two-person award, but the priority questions around Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum and the overlap with the 2008 prize remain unresolved. I rank it above no award. No award is last, because both proposals describe achievements that meet the maturity and attribution tests.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; I have no co-authorship or institutional tie to Autor, Dorn, Hanson, Helpman or Melitz. I disclose methodological affinity, since my own work uses quasi-experimental designs in labour economics, and that the 2021 Scientific Background cites my class-size paper.
